scenarios.name: Baseline Control
scenarios.description: v7.1 baseline / v7.2 energy baseline regression. A should retain comparative advantage in Metal while B should develop comparative advantage in Electronics. Expected qualitative result: Metal A->B and Electronics B->A coexist through the same transport sector. In v7.2 shared energy should remain unconstrained in normal equilibrium: fulfillment ratios near 1, unserved energy near 0, and endogenous energy price near local generation cost. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: Timed B Reactivation
scenarios.description: Baseline develops until day 360. From day 360 to 720 transport cost rises sharply. B should first reactivate mothballed refinery capacity; new installed capacity should only appear if the remaining installed reserve is genuinely insufficient. After day 720 cheap imports return and B should mothball again. In v6.3, watch Activation Queue and Strategic Reserve before Surplus is committed to decommissioning. v7.0.1 also verifies that freight already contracted before the freight-cost shock is not repriced in transit. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: Timed Transport Demand Surge
scenarios.description: Baseline develops until day 360. B metal demand doubles from day 360 to 720. Transport should first activate mothballed capacity, then construct new installed capacity only if needed. In v7.2 this scenario also serves as the Metal energy-demand surge test: higher A metal output should raise A requested energy and, if generation is exceeded, create scarcity, higher energy price, and cost/trade feedback. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: Timed Low Demand Rationalization
scenarios.description: Baseline develops until day 360. B demand falls to 55% from day 360 to 720. Active refinery and transport capacity should mothball quickly while installed capacity retires slowly. When demand returns, mothballed capacity should reactivate before new construction. In v6.3, low demand should first create Strategic Reserve and Surplus; Surplus then enters a separate decommissioning queue and only later becomes Retired. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: Timed Reverse Advantage
scenarios.description: Baseline develops until day 360. From day 360 onward Metal comparative advantage is moved from A to B. r4 deliberately grants B ample test-only generation headroom during this legacy regression so the test still isolates Metal trade reversal and capital response instead of being dominated by the new v7.2 power bottleneck. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: Timed Electronics Demand Surge
scenarios.description: Baseline develops until day 360. A electronics demand doubles from day 360 to 720. Electronics B->A trade and B electronics production should rise; shared transport remains common with Metal. In v7.2 this scenario also serves as the Electronics energy-demand surge test: higher B electronics output should raise B requested energy and, if generation is exceeded, create scarcity, higher energy price, and cost/trade feedback. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: Timed Reverse Electronics Advantage
scenarios.description: Baseline develops until day 360. From day 360 onward Electronics comparative advantage is moved from B to A. r4 deliberately grants A ample test-only generation headroom during this legacy regression so the test still isolates Electronics trade reversal while Metal remains an independent commodity regression. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: Timed Two-Good Transport Surge
scenarios.description: Baseline develops until day 360. From day 360 to 720 B metal demand and A electronics demand both rise. The two opposite-direction commodity flows should compete for one shared transport capacity. In v7.0 rationing is proportional to requested transport load; value-based cargo priority is intentionally absent. In v7.1 the equal proportional fulfillment of v7.0 should disappear during genuine scarcity: the lane with the larger positive trade surplus per transport-equivalent unit should receive priority. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: Timed Metal Priority Scarcity
scenarios.description: Dedicated v7.1 allocator reversal test. Baseline develops until day 360. From day 360 to 720, B metal demand and A electronics demand both rise, while B ore cost is sharply increased. Both commodity lanes should compete for scarce shared transport, but metal A->B should now have higher trade surplus per transport-equivalent unit than electronics B->A and therefore receive the higher fulfillment share. After day 720 the system should return toward the normal baseline. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: v7.2 Simultaneous Two-Industry Energy Shortage
scenarios.description: Timed Test Mode=9. From day 360 to 720 B metal demand and A electronics demand are both multiplied by the dedicated energy-stress multiplier. This should make A metal plus A import-substitution electronics compete for the same A power capacity; diagnostics must show both requested-energy lanes and proportional physical rationing when scarcity occurs. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: v7.2 Cheap-Energy Comparative Advantage
scenarios.description: Timed Test Mode=10. From day 360 onward A generation cost falls sharply while B generation cost rises sharply. No trade direction is hard-coded; commodity costs, landed prices and trade should react endogenously to the changed energy-cost geography. This is intentionally strong so the effect is observable despite existing feedstock/labor differences. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: v7.2 Generation Capacity Shock Recovery
scenarios.description: Timed Test Mode=11. From day 360 to 720 A active generation capacity is cut to 60% of installed capacity, then restored instantly. Requested energy, physical fulfillment, endogenous energy price, Metal/Electronics output and trade should react during the outage and relax after day 720. [v7.3 regression freeze: Electronics/Energy capital lifecycle disabled to preserve the accepted v7.2 r4 reference behavior.]

scenarios.name: v7.3 Lifecycle Baseline
scenarios.description: No exogenous shock. Electronics and Energy capital lifecycle enabled. This is the new normal-operation baseline: one-time rationalization from inherited fixed-capacity initial conditions is allowed, but the system must settle without self-excited construction/mothball cycles; commodity/trade directions must remain economically coherent.

scenarios.name: v7.3 Temporary Electronics Reactivation
scenarios.description: Lifecycle enabled. A electronics local base demand doubles from day 360 to 720. A should use mothballed installed factory capital first; construction may occur only if the retained installed reserve is insufficient. After day 720 demand returns and excess active factory/power capacity should mothball rather than disappear instantly.

scenarios.name: v7.3 Sustained Electronics Growth
scenarios.description: Lifecycle enabled. A electronics local base demand rises 4x permanently from day 360. Existing inactive factory capacity should reactivate first; persistent structural shortage should then construct new Electronics installed capacity. Higher electronics output should also induce endogenous A generation-capital expansion after the longer power planning/construction delay.

scenarios.name: v7.3 Electronics Collapse and Recovery
scenarios.description: Lifecycle enabled. B electronics local demand falls to 35% from day 360 to 720, then recovers. B factory active capacity and generation active capital should mothball during the collapse and reactivate on recovery; permanent retirement should be much slower than operational mothballing.

scenarios.name: v7.3 Sustained Metal Driven Power Growth
scenarios.description: Lifecycle enabled. B metal demand doubles permanently from day 360. Existing refinery/transport mechanisms respond as before; the resulting sustained industrial load should propagate into A power planning and new installed generation construction, demonstrating that Energy capital responds to demand from another sector rather than only Electronics.

scenarios.name: v7.4 Intermediate Inputs Baseline
scenarios.description: Coupled baseline with Metal as the physical Electronics intermediate input. No exogenous shock; used to verify going-concern behavior and the new physical/cost channels.

scenarios.name: v7.4 Temporary Metal Supply Shock
scenarios.description: Coupled economy. A mining capacity is reduced to 50% from day 360 to 720; the Metal supply shock should propagate through trade into Electronics cost/output and then recover.

scenarios.name: v7.4 Sustained Electronics Growth with Input Coupling
scenarios.description: Coupled economy. A Electronics local base demand rises 4x permanently from day 360, testing Metal input demand, refinery expansion and induced power-capital growth.

scenarios.name: v7.4 Coupled Metal Demand Growth
scenarios.description: Coupled economy. B final Metal local base demand doubles permanently from day 360, testing proportional competition between final and intermediate Metal demand and refinery adaptation.

scenarios.name: v7.5 Capital Goods Baseline
scenarios.description: Coupled economy with capital goods enabled. Refinery, Electronics and Power expansion in both colonies consume locally produced capital goods.

scenarios.name: v7.5 Capital Goods Supply Shock
scenarios.description: Capital-goods sector enabled. Colony A capital-goods production capacity is multiplied by 0.1 from day 360 through 720; B remains unshocked.

scenarios.name: v7.5 Investment Boom
scenarios.description: Capital-goods sector enabled. Colony A electronics local demand is multiplied by 4 from day 360 onward, creating simultaneous capital-goods demand from expansion.

scenarios.name: v7.5.1 Transport Capital Goods Closure
scenarios.description: Capital Goods and intermediate inputs enabled. Shared Transport expansion is physically backed by A/B Capital Goods inventories; the legacy temporary transport-demand surge is reused to force observable Transport investment.

scenarios.name: v7.6 Energy Resource Supply Shock
scenarios.description: Energy Kernel v2 enabled. A primary power-resource extraction is reduced to 50% during the standard temporary test window while generation capital remains intact; validates resource-limited generation and recovery.

scenarios.name: v7.6 Energy Capacity-Only Control Shock
scenarios.description: Energy Kernel v2 enabled. A active generation capacity is temporarily reduced while primary resource extraction remains normal; distinguishes capacity scarcity from operating-resource scarcity.

scenarios.name: v7.7 Construction Materials Baseline
scenarios.description: Full coupled economy with Construction Materials enabled and no v7.7 supply shock.

scenarios.name: v7.7 Construction Materials Supply Shock
scenarios.description: Construction Materials enabled. Colony A processing capacity is multiplied by the v7.7 Construction Materials Shock Multiplier during the standard temporary test window; B remains unshocked.

scenarios.name: v7.7 Regolith Supply Shock
scenarios.description: Construction Materials enabled. Colony A Regolith extraction capacity is multiplied by the v7.7 Regolith Shock Multiplier during the standard temporary test window; B remains unshocked.

scenarios.name: v7.7.1 Transport Construction Materials Baseline
scenarios.description: Full coupled v7.7 economy with shared Transport Construction Materials enabled and no additional stimulus.

scenarios.name: v7.7.1 Transport Surge on Construction Materials
scenarios.description: Full coupled v7.7 economy with shared Transport Construction Materials enabled; reuses the standard temporary Transport-demand surge to stimulate colony B.
